audience.programmeDescription: Delft’s Electrical Engineering bachelor combines mathematics and physics with circuits, signals, digital systems, telecommunications and electrical energy. Integrated projects develop electrical-system design and experimentation; a minor and graduation project complete the degree.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial study in signals, mathematical systems, robotics, computing and renewable energy. These can support related technical interests, but they do not combine into a sustained programme in electrical devices, circuits and electrical-system design. A full UCR comparison is therefore not offered.

curriculum.limitation: The 30-EC minor remains open, subject to approval and overlap rules. Two distinct 5-EC electives are selected across years two and three. The 15-EC graduation project requires completion of all first- and second-year courses.

components: Electrical Engineering for the Next Generation

Year 3. Genuine approved 30-EC minor; must not overlap the two selected EEX courses.

exception.reason: Delft integrates electrical physics, circuits, semiconductor devices, signals, communications and energy through repeated electrical-system design and experiments. UCR provides substantial signals, mathematical systems, robotics, computing and energy study, but the tested combination does not sustain that physical-electrical analysis and design formation.
exception.curriculumContext: The complete 180-EC Delft curriculum is retained, including a 30-EC minor, two distinct 5-EC restricted electives and a 15-EC graduation project.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: A complete feasible candidate was tested with Linear Systems, Robotics, Energy & Sustainability, Renewable System Design and Consumer Product Design, alongside mathematics, networks, algorithms and machine learning. Its real technical strengths do not establish a sustained curriculum in electrical circuits, device behaviour and electrical-system experimentation and design.

candidateAssessment.concept: Computational signals, autonomous systems and renewable energy
candidateAssessment.assessment: Genuine signals/control, robot manipulation, energy-system analysis and product-design methods were tested together. Their recurring work remains computational modelling and energy assessment rather than integrated electrical-system design and testing.

candidateAssessment.concept: Computational systems andneuroscience for medical technology
candidateAssessment.assessment: Neurobiology, perception and cognitive experiments provide substantive biological study. They do not implement medical electronics, implant engineering or physiological-instrument design.
Logic, mathematics and wave/material science provide partial foundations. They do not form a circuit, semiconductor and electromagnetic-device design sequence.
